title: What Scripture forbids: acts of religious adoration toward creatures under any pretext
source_text: LXXII. Verum Scriptura sacra, dum creaturas adorare & illis servire prohibet, non vetat simpliciter ne creaturas agnoscamus ut primum principium atque ultimum finem, easque sub hac ratione colamus; sed ne quovis praetextu exerceamus erga illas adorationis religiosae actus, quales sunt aliquem publice invocare, hymnos illi canere, incensum adolere, aedes sacras & festos dies dicare, per nomen ejus jurare, vota illi nuncupare, & quae sunt similia.
pass_a_gloss: But sacred Scripture, while it forbids to adore creatures and to serve them, does not simply forbid that we acknowledge creatures as first principle and last end and worship them under this aspect; but that under any pretext whatever we exercise toward them acts of religious adoration, such as are: to invoke someone publicly, to sing hymns to him, to burn incense, to dedicate sacred buildings and feast days, to swear by his name, to vow vows to him, and the things which are similar.
pass_b_english: When Holy Scripture forbids us to adore creatures and serve them, it is not merely ruling out that we should take creatures for the first principle and last end and worship them in that capacity. It rules out our performing, on any pretext at all, acts of religious adoration toward them: calling on someone in public worship, singing him hymns, burning incense, dedicating churches and feast days, swearing by his name, making vows to him, and the like.

choices.why: Sacred buildings dedicated in someone's honor; in seventeenth-century controversy these are churches and chapels.
